newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Euroshares hit records, Lebed nerves fade.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Euroshares hit records, Lebed nerves fade.

text.p: Europe's key bourses advanced across a broad front on Friday, carrying the British and German stock markets to new closing highs after the Lebed factor waned.
The markets rose unanimously, taking their cue from Wall Street's surge to its 30th record close of the year on Thursday.
They had no trouble dispelling nervousness which followed the sacking by Russia's President Boris Yeltsin of his security chief, Alexander Lebed, on Thursday.
"The Russian situation isn't as bad as we thought," said one German share dealer.

British shares closed at a record high for the third time in five sessions, buoyed by firm U.S. Treasury bonds and lifted towards the close as the Dow Jones industrial average recovered from early losses following weaker-than-expected U.S. trade figures.
The U.S. trade deficit was $10.83 billion in August, compared with $11.6 billion in July.

London's FTSE 100 share index closed 11.0 points higher at 4,053.1, surpassing its previous record close of 4,050.8 set October 15. Traders and fund managers said shares could continue higher as long as U.S. markets advance, despite recent strong British economic figures suggesting a growing inflation risk.
"There just seems to be so much underlying energy in the U.S. markets," said Michael Lenhoff, head of research at fund management group Capel-Cure Myers.

"If interest rates stay where they are, the markets could go even more ballistic but we are in for a nasty shock when rates change. All the conventional measures are looking stretched in the U.S. and as soon as the interest rate backdrop changes, you could find a lot of people dashing for the same door at once."
On the eve of the ninth anniversary of the crash of 1987, some traders said markets could yet see the sharp losses which have a knack of hitting the market in October.
At 1600 GMT, the Dow Jones industrial average of U.S. shares was down 7.09 points.
In Frankfurt, investors in German shares who sold in late floor trading on Thursday after Lebed's sacking hurried back into the market on Friday, traders said.
The German DAX index of 30 leading shares ended floor trade up alnost 0.7 percent at a new record close of 2,734.82 points.

Economists said the idea that the German economy was more exposed than other Western economies at times of Russian political stress -- in both geographical and trade terms -- held less significance than it used to do.
Klaus Baader, senior currency economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, said Russia's relations with the West were on a much more multilateral basis, compared with the early 1990s.
In Paris the blue-chip CAC-40 index rose to its highest close since May 1994, up 19.90 points or 0.92 percent at 2,185.23.
In currencies, the dollar closed little chagned against the mark but gained ground versus the yen as the Japanese currency suffered a fresh bout of weakness, dealers said.
Initial dollar sales after the release of the U.S. trade data were reversed as the dollar found support below 1.54 marks.
"The dollar recovered quickly after the data," said Merita Bank's Alan Collins.
Analysts said dollar/yen had pushed to a fresh 33-month high at 112.63 yen earlier as dealers seemed eager to test the Bank of Japan's patience with a stronger dollar/yen.

Sterling rose to 2.4568 marks, its highest since December 1994, on a newspaper report that a member of the British Treasury's panel of independent economic advisers, Tim Congdon, said Britain should raise official interest rates by a full percentage point from 5.75 percent.
CURRENCIES AT 1600 GMT
The dollar was trading at 1.5420 marks and 112.55 yen compared with 1.5436 and 112.25 in late European business on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS CLOSING PRICES
London - The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares ended 11.0 points higher at 4,053.1.
Paris - the CAC-40 share index finished up 19.90 at 2,185.23.
Frankfurt - The 30-share DAX index closed up 18.56 at 2,734.82. In post bourse trading the Ibis DAX was at 2,727.56 in electronic trading.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed European trading at $380.15 an ounce after ending at $380.45 on Thursday.
